args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failing health checks, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api deployed v2.3.1 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks, with error rate at 18% and healthy=false across all regions.

Action taken: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc was not eligible — it is unhealthy and only in staging.)

Note: The first rollback attempt partially failed — the orchestrator halted after us-east, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout to all three regions.

Current state: All regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 0.2%.

Follow-up: Root cause analysis of v2.3.1 still needed before any redeploy; the v2.3.1 rollout should be treated as blocked until investigated.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did get created (INC-0001) despite the timeout — no retry needed, so the on-call engineer wasn't paged twice.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was running v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), failing health checks with an 18% error rate.

**Rollback target:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release marked healthy in production. I deliberately excluded `v2.3.1-rc`: it's unhealthy *and* only deployed to staging, so it was never a healthy production release. v2.3.0 had prior production health, so no change-manager approval was required.

**Rollback execution:** The first attempt partially failed — the orchestrator halted after us-east, leaving a split state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1). I verified the actual per-region state rather than trusting the error message, then retried, which completed the rollout.

**Final state:** All three regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 0.2%.

**Incident:** INC-0001 opened at SEV2 with the full timeline. Note the create call timed out at 30s, but I confirmed via `list_incidents` that it had in fact succeeded before doing anything else — worth knowing that this tool can report a timeout on an operation that actually committed.

**Follow-up worth flagging:** v2.3.1 should stay blocked pending root-cause analysis. Also, that partial-rollback failure is a real reliability gap — an orchestrator halt mid-rollout leaves a split-version fleet, and the error surface ("partial_failure") isn't obviously actionable without a follow-up status check. That may deserve its own ticket.
